# Browser components bundled with Canvas Desk 1.4.0

Canvas Desk is MIT licensed. The browser helper is a separate process and contains these third-party components:

| Component | Version | License |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JCEF Maven | 152.0.6 | Apache-2.0 |
| Java Chromium Embedded Framework API | jcef-17e805a / CEF 152.0.6 / Chromium 152.0.7977.83 | BSD-style JCEF license |
| JOGL (transitive API and renderer libraries) | v2.4.0 | BSD-2/BSD-3, SGI Free Software License B 2.0, Apache-1.1/2.0, Ubuntu Font License 1.0; full upstream terms included |
| GlueGen runtime (transitive) | v2.4.0 | BSD-2/BSD-3 and Apache-2.0; full upstream terms included |
| Gson | 2.11.0 | Apache-2.0 |
| Commons Compress | 1.28.0 | Apache-2.0 |
| Commons Codec | 1.19.0 | Apache-2.0 |
| Commons IO | 2.20.0 | Apache-2.0 |
| Commons Lang | 3.18.0 | Apache-2.0 |
| Error Prone annotations | 2.27.0 | Apache-2.0 |

License texts and the Apache component notices from the original artifacts are in `licenses/browser/`, included in the mod and helper JARs. JCEF API's copyright/disclaimer is preserved in its LICENSE.txt.

The native Chromium/CEF runtime is downloaded separately from the JCEF Maven 152.0.6 release, verified against the publisher SHA-256 values pinned in `native-sha256.json`. Its own LICENSE.txt and third-party notices remain in the installed runtime. No native Chromium/CEF browser binary is included in the mod JAR. The transitive JOGL/GlueGen packages include renderer JNI libraries for their supported platforms; they stay inside the helper resource, outside the Minecraft classloader. CanvasBrowser uses its custom OSR sink without creating a JOGL window. Unmodified upstream license texts are from https://github.com/sgothel/jogl/tree/v2.4.0 and https://github.com/sgothel/gluegen/tree/v2.4.0 . Sources: https://github.com/jcefmaven/jcefmaven and https://github.com/chromiumembedded/java-cef . YouTube integration uses https://developers.google.com/youtube/iframe_api_reference .

The validation fixture generated by tools/prepare-media-fixture.py is a local synthetic color pattern with no audio track. The earlier optional MDN flower fixture is CC0 and is not redistributed in this release.
